=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml: lines 1534-1539 (the perl `$neg` suppression block) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The continuation-line suppression pattern `next if /^\s{2,}\S/;` requires at least 2 spaces of indentation. A continuation line indented with exactly 1 space (e.g. a list item continuation that happens to use a single-space indent) would not be suppressed and would instead reset `$neg` to 0, causing the remaining negative-list items to be printed and scanned as edit targets.
  WHY: If a plan author formats a wrapped list item continuation in the negative sublist with a single leading space instead of two, the suppression state is prematurely exited. The subsequent negative-list items (still semantically part of the "No changes are expected to" list) would then be printed to the files section and would be scanned by the guard as template-owned edit targets, re-creating the false-positive failure the fix is meant to eliminate.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml: line 2219 (`BLOCKED_ALREADY_SATISFIED_REGEX` assignment) | severity=NIT | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The new regex branch `(validation|verification)[- ]only` lacks word-boundary anchors (`\<...\>`) unlike the existing real-obstacle regex.
  WHY: A BLOCKED verdict containing a compound word like "prevalidation-only-failure" could match "validation-only" as a substring, incorrectly classifying a real failure as a success-no-op if no real-obstacle term also appears.

  PROBLEM: The new `(validation|verification)[- ]only` branch is unanchored — it matches the literal substring anywhere in the BLOCKED verdict. Verdicts that negate the validation-only claim (e.g., "BLOCKED: This isn't validation only; the change is real and significant." or "BLOCKED: We are not at validation only; code edits are needed.") contain "validation only" as a substring and therefore match the new branch, but they do not contain any of the obstacle keywords (`\<cannot\>`, `\<unavailable\>`, `\<denied\>`, etc.), so the BLOCKED_REAL_OBSTACLE_REGEX veto never fires.
  WHY: A model that wants to refuse the no-op classification (because real changes are needed) but uses a negation form gets caught by the new branch anyway. The issue is then closed or moved to `ai:closed` via the no-op path, sending a working issue back to a human or prematurely closing an orchestrator-managed phase.

  WHY: A prose paragraph in the middle of a "No changes are expected to:" section that mentions a path via inline backticks can re-enable scanning, placing that path in `FILES_SECTION_FILE`, causing the guard to fail on a path the plan explicitly named as unchanged.
